entities.text: Nawab Basir Yar Jung Villayat Manjil
entities.label: PETITIONER

sentences.text: This petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India has been filed against order dated 09.12.2000 passed by Ninth Additional District Judge, Bhopal in Land Acquisition Misc. Property Case No.3/99 by which application filed by petitioner under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act has been rejected on the ground of maintainability.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Misc. Property Case No.3/99
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: 2. It is submitted by counsel for petitioner that for the benefit of petitioner the land was acquired.
However, petitioner is aggrieved by quantum of compensation fixed by L.A.O., therefore, an application under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act was filed for reference.
However, by impugned order the said application has been rejected on the ground of maintainability.

By referring to Sections 15, 18 and 25 of Land Acquisition Act, it is submitted by counsel for petitioner that before adjudicating the quantum of compensation, L.A.O. should have heard the petitioner.

3. Heard learned counsel for parties.
4.
The moot question for consideration is as to whether an application under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act is maintainable on behalf of beneficiary or Government.
5. The question is no more res integra.

6. The Supreme Court in the case of Santosh Kumar and others v. Central Warehousing Corporation and another, reported in (1986) 2 SCC 343 had held as under:
"4.

entities.text: Santosh Kumar and others v. Central Warehousing Corporation and another, reported in (1986) 2 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In our view there cannot be any possible doubt that the scheme of the Act is that,
apart from fraud, corruption or collusion, the amount of compensation awarded by the Collector under Section 11 of the Act may not be questioned in any proceeding either by the government or by the company or local authority at whose instance the acquisition is made. Section 50(2) and Section 25 lead to that inevitable conclusion.

Surely what may not be done under the provisions of the Act may not be permitted to M.P. Power Transmission Company Ltd. vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154019167/
2 be done by invoking the jurisdiction of the High Court under Article 226.

entities.text: M.P. Power Transmission Company Ltd. vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 10 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Article 226 is not meant to avoid or circumvent the processes of the law and the provisions of the statute.

When Section 50(2) expressly bars the company or local authority at whose instance the acquisition is made from demanding a reference under Section 18 of the Act, notwithstanding that such company or local authority may be allowed to adduce evidence before the Collector, and when Section 25 expressly prohibits the court from reducing the amount of compensation while dealing with the reference under Section 18, it is clearly not permissible for the company or local authority to invoke the jurisdiction of the High Court under Article 226to challenge the amount of compensation awarded by the Collector and to have it reduced.
5. Long ago, it was held in Ezra v. Secy. of State for India [(1904-5) 32 IA 93 : 1905 ILR 32 Cal 605 : 9 CWN 454] , and it has never been doubted since, "that the "award"
in which the enquiry by the Collector results is merely a decision (binding only on the Collector) as to what sum shall be tendered to the owners of the lands" and that, "if a judicial ascertainment of value is desired by the owner, he can obtain it by requiring the matter to be referred by the Collector to the court".

entities.text: Ezra v. Secy. of State for India [(1904-5) 32 IA 93 : 1905 ILR 32 Cal 605 : 9 CWN 454]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As pointed out by this Court in Raja Harish Chandra v. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer [AIR 1961 SC 1500 :
(1962) 1 SCR 676] , the observations of the Privy Council in Ezra case [(1904- 5) 32 IA 93 : 1905 ILR 32 Cal 605 : 9 CWN 454] indicate that the Collector, in making an award, acts as an agent of the Government, and that the legal character of the award made by the Collector is that of a tender or offer by him on behalf of the Government.

entities.text:
Raja Harish Chandra v. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer [AIR 1961 SC 1500 :
(1962) 1 SCR 676]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (See also Mohammad Hasnuddin v. State of Maharashtra [(1979) 2 SCC 572 : (1979) 2 SCR 265, 274] .)

entities.text: Mohammad Hasnuddin v. State of Maharashtra [(1979) 2 SCC 572 : (1979) 2 SCR 265, 274]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If the Collector making an award was in law making an offer on behalf of the Government, it is difficult to appreciate how the Government or anyone who could but (sic put) claim through the Government would be entitled to question the award, apart from fraud, corruption or collusion."
7.
Accordingly, this Court is of considered opinion that reference Court did not commit any mistake by rejecting the application filed under Section 18 of Land Acquisition Act as not maintainable.
8. Accordingly, the petition fails and is hereby dismissed.
